title: JANUS Engine — magnetic commutation selection screen for Axle
purpose: Numerically test whether repeated magnetic-state cancellation is compatible with the low-power JANUS Axle budget and quantify the starter-generator torque envelope before detailed electromagnetic geometry exists.

closed_cycle_energy_test.active_cancel_case: If a coil supplies -tau_PM over the negative half-cycle, coil mechanical work is +2*tau_pk, while net shaft work over the full cycle becomes +2*tau_pk.
closed_cycle_energy_test.result: The apparent net shaft work equals the work supplied by the active cancelling field in the ideal limit; real copper, inverter and magnetic losses make electrical input larger. Therefore selective cancellation is torque shaping, not energy multiplication.

electropermanent_per_sector_budget.literature_scale_check: A published VFMM pulse-trajectory experiment reported re/de-magnetization operation losses of roughly 33.58 J and 27.88 J for one specific machine and pulse strategy. Those values are not transferable to JANUS dimensions, but they are far above the per-event energy ceiling that a low-power per-sector JANUS scheme would require at hundreds of RPM.
electropermanent_per_sector_budget.verdict: DO_NOT_USE_EPM_MAGNETIZATION_STATE_SWITCHING_EVERY_SECTOR. Use EPM/VFMM only for infrequent persistent mode changes if a later subsystem benefits.

coreless_AFPM_power_to_torque_screen.interpretation: The current JANUS low-tens-of-watts electrical scale corresponds to sub-Nm to about 1.1 Nm shaft torque in the 300-600 RPM range. That is a tractable first electromagnetic bench target; 60 RPM requires much larger torque for the same power and is a less attractive baseline unless the Axle hydrodynamics demand it.

selected_test_article.preferred_installation: dry-side or magnetically coupled across non-ferromagnetic low-eddy-current boundary
selected_test_article.baseline_control: position sensor + three-phase inverter + FOC/synchronous commutation
operating_modes: START: battery supplies positive Axle torque
ASSIST: controller supplies only the torque needed to hold target RPM
COAST: zero commanded torque to measure native Axle drag
REGEN: if real hydraulic/mechanical input drives Axle above command, inverter returns electrical energy to DC bus/battery
RIPPLE_TRIM: inject only the minimum measured harmonic compensation current if residual torque ripple matters

R0M1_measurements: no-current breakaway torque and drag torque versus RPM
motor electrical-to-shaft efficiency map at 60/120/300/600 RPM
temperature rise in coils and magnets
eddy-current drag with the intended chamber/barrier material
battery energy used during startup and recovered during regen

pass_conditions.energy: Integrated motor/assist electrical energy must be charged to the battery/DC bus; regen credited only from independently identified mechanical input.
pass_conditions.cogging: No-current magnetic drag/cogging must be small compared with native Axle hydrodynamic/scale-management torque.
pass_conditions.startup: Starter-generator must reach target Axle RPM within the allowed battery startup envelope without overheating.
pass_conditions.self_drive: After JANUS reaches steady state, battery-neutral/self-drive may be claimed only if SOC does not decrease over the declared hold window after all active auxiliaries and magnetic-drive electronics are included.

verdict.why: It solves the actual JANUS need—startup, controlled rotation and regeneration—without deliberately introducing a magnetic braking barrier that later has to be electrically cancelled.
verdict.EPM_role: reserve for rare persistent state switching, latches or valves, not Axle pole-by-pole commutation
